repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
    wait until(not ((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true))
    fired = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR uses a rising-edge wait (`wait(Motion == true, rising)`), which fires only when the motion sensor transitions from false to true. The candidate uses a periodic `if` (`if (motion == true)`), which only evaluates the condition at the start of each 1-second cycle. At t=100ms, the sensor became true, but the candidate's `if` guard was false at that instant, so it did nothing. The candidate also incorrectly sets `triggered = false` in the `else` branch, which would prevent re-firing if the condition were to become true again.
changed_locations: Line 2: changed operator from `==` to `==|` is not needed here as binding is single device; changed structure from periodic `if` to blocking two-wait rearm pattern
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling `if` with a blocking rising-edge state machine. Added a `fired` flag to track if the rising edge has been processed in the current cycle. Added `wait until(not (motion))` to block until the sensor returns to false (rearming), then `wait until(motion)` to block until it becomes true, execute the body, and set `fired = true`. This ensures the action fires exactly at the rising edge and waits for the next rising edge on the subsequent cycle.
